title: Approximate maximum flow from shortest paths via multiplicative edge-length updates

difficulty_reason: The complete five-part analysis couples a path-packing primal iterate to multiplicatively updated dual edge lengths. Its load-bearing core is the shifted dual certificate (ell_i-ell_0)/(d_i-delta*n), the exact accumulated weighted-length increment, and the auxiliary h_i recurrence bounding d_i by delta*n*exp(val(f_i)/beta). Combining that bound with stopping, congestion control, and delta=n^(-1/epsilon) gives a capacity-respecting (1-O(epsilon))-maximum flow in O(m*log(n)/epsilon^2) shortest-path calls. These intermediate potential/dual arguments are worked by the author, not assumed as an external theorem. Parts1,2,5 alone are elementary estimates and are not separate H2 claims. Root confirmed H2 for the complete chain after actual five-page source review and focused semantic comparison.
statement_scope: Q4 parts1-5 in full: the directed-capacity shortest-path multiplicative edge-length algorithm, iteration and congestion bounds, shifted feasible dual lengths, flow-value lower bound, and parameter choice yielding a capacity-respecting (1-O(epsilon))-maximum s-t flow in O(m*log(n)/epsilon^2) shortest-path calls; retain original 0<epsilon,delta<1/2, u(e)>=1, and strict stopping test.

source_caveats: Both full originalPDFs are retained separately. Q4 exact statement physical2–3 and solution physical4–6; earlier initial scope[2,5] was corrected to include6 on actual-source evidence.

Official solution Q4 is individually signed Antti Roeyskoe; statement authorship is attributed only at course level to Bernhard Haeupler, Johannes Lengler and Maximilian Probst. No separately named worksheet writer is claimed.

The original stopping test is dist_{ell_{i-1}}(s,t)>1, not >=1. Solution part1 says an edge of length1 or greater cannot occur on a chosen path and gives a ceiling count; equality1 can still occur. This can affect a unit/additive iteration boundary, while the requested O(m*ln(1/delta)/epsilon) bound is unchanged. The original is retained.

Solution part4 bottom of physical p5 switches among d_t,d_{t+1},d_k while setting i=k; the final displayed logarithm uses d_k. Root should preserve and assess this notation caveat against the exact loop stopping convention.

The source does not separately discuss beta=0 (no s-t path), whereas the proof divides by beta; the algorithm then terminates without augmenting. This is disclosed as a degenerate-case omission, with no new hypothesis inserted into the statement.
The full Q4 permits using earlier parts even if unsolved. The proposed primary scope includes all1-5; no independent count is requested for its elementary subparts.

The current 2025 lecture notes are on Moodle and may change; the official page publicly links older notes but those are not a fixed substitute. No third PDF was acquired. Q4 restates its algorithm, parameters, LP dual and strong-duality equality in the two selected statement pages, so it needs no course-specific omitted lemma.
